name: esp32_c3_zero
title: Waveshare ESP32-C3-Zero
description: A small ESP32-C3 board: 4 MB flash in the chip, castellated holes, USB-C to the chip, a WS2812B, BOOT and RESET buttons, a ceramic antenna
notes: USB-C goes to the chip itself, GPIO 18 and 19: no USB bridge, the log comes on the USB Serial/JTAG port. GPIO 18 and 19 also come out on holes; wired to something else they take the USB away.
The WS2812B on GPIO 10 is fed from 5V, so its data input wants more than the 3.3 V of the pin. Not tried on the board.
TX and RX are GPIO 21 and 20, UART0.

usb.notes: The USB-C: D- and D+ go to the USB Serial/JTAG of the chip (UD_N on IO18, UD_P on IO19), the console and the flashing.

reg_3v3.notes: An LDO from 5V to VCC3.3; the product page of Waveshare names an ME6217C33M5G.

power.name: 5V
power.why: VBUS of the USB-C, also on the 5V hole.

header.type: castellated holes, 2.54 mm, 18 along two edges

front.source: a photo by Anton of his board, 2026-11-06

back.source: a photo by Anton of his board, 2026-11-02

connectors.source: Header 20 of the schematic; the labels of the holes on the photo of the back of Anton's board

flash.source: the product page of Waveshare: an ESP32-C3 with 4 MB flash in the package

antenna.source: ANT1 through R221, 0 ohm, no connector; a ceramic chip on the photo. quality by the marks of data-format.md

antenna_rssi.by: rssi_probe on Anton's desk, one access point on channel 1, 60 s each
antenna_rssi.notes: Median RSSI on its pins, face down: -60 dBm at 0 and -64 at 90 degrees; face up, flat on the desk: -64 at 0 degrees.

edges.source: the labels of the holes on the photos of both sides of Anton's board, front.webp and back.webp: on the front USB-C is on the left, and the back is the board turned over about its vertical axis
